events.title: Lisle's clerks bind the agreements in one book
events.body: Arthur Lisle's two clerks spend the winter at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir copying every agreement made between the island and the strangers since the leave, with Cairt na Companaidh bound at the back. Lisle reads the book through with a pen and writes his queries in the margins; the letter-books keep forty pages of his notes.

events.title: The hawk-faithful carry the customs officer out of Ros gheal
events.body: Eleven days after the customs house opens, some thirty hawk-faithful of Ros gheal come down from the hawk-house at dusk, carry the officer's table, book and scale into the street, and walk him to the last house on the road south. He returns within the month with two clerks and a letter from Lisle.

events.title: Ros gheal rows the customs officer down the coast
events.body: At the autumn herring the fishing families of Ros gheal put the customs officer, his clerks, his table and his scale into a boat and set them ashore on a roadless beach two miles down the coast. The town's roll says only that he went away by water. Lisle writes that the town has broken no page, since none yet binds it.

events.title: Ùna finds no silver in Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg
events.body: Reading the council's copies by rushlight at the inns of Rathad na Mèinne on her way home, Ùna nic Choinnich finds coal named on every page of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg and no word of silver, nor of any metal but the iron the humans paid with. At the inn below Muileann chrom she tells her grandson that A' Chompanaidh holds no paper for the seam.

events.title: Ùna nic Choinnich calls the guild to the hall
events.body: The agent of A' Chompanaidh at Muileann chrom sends notice to Muileann chiar that surveyors will measure the silver seam in spring under the charter's first refusal. Ùna nic Choinnich reads the letter in both tongues to forty-one members of Comann an Airgid gathered in the guild hall by night, and resolves to ask the council what it holds.

events.title: Coinneach Glas lends Ùna the council's copies
events.body: Ùna nic Choinnich rides three days to Cathair dhearg. Coinneach Glas, Ceann a' Chùraim, aged sixty-eight and ailing, hears her out in the room of the rolls and gives her the council's own copies of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg, Puingean a' Chalaidh and the pit contracts, bidding her look for the silver before the humans do.

events.title: The surveyor's report reaches Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir
events.body: The chief surveyor reports to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir that the whole of Muileann chiar met him at the working, silent, and that he found no grant or payment to A' Chompanaidh in either of the guild's books and did not think it prudent to proceed. Lisle writes beneath it that he would not have found it either, and sends for the bound book.

events.title: Lisle writes that the charter gives A' Chompanaidh nothing
events.body: In a long letter to the master of A' Chompanaidh, Arthur Lisle sets out that Cairt na Companaidh is a promise made by its own masters and grants nothing on the island, where the only title is Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg, which speaks of coal and says nothing of silver. The master of A' Chompanaidh protests; Lisle answers in two lines.

events.title: The guild asks for the compact in both tongues
events.body: Answering Lisle's proposal of a compact, Ùna nic Choinnich writes in the humans' letters that the guild will sign, that it must be signed at Muileann chiar where the seam lies, and that it be written in both tongues line against line. Lisle strikes out his clerk's query and agrees, and says he will come himself on Là Fhèill Brìde.

events.title: The council's copies returned from Muileann chiar
events.body: In the spring after the compact Ùna nic Choinnich sends the council's leaves of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg, Puingean a' Chalaidh and the pit contracts back to Cathair dhearg by her grandson Fionnlagh, wrapped in the same oilcloth they came in, with a bar of silver for the clerk who keeps the presses.

events.title: The compact read in the guild hall
events.body: On the evening of the signing, after Lisle's carriage has gone down the valley, Cùmhnant an Airgid is read aloud to Comann an Airgid in the guild hall of Muileann chiar from its Dia-thìris column, and read a second time for the apprentices. It is laid that night in the guild chest under three locks.

events.title: Lisle sees the silver seam
events.body: Before leaving Muileann chiar Arthur Lisle asks to see the seam, and Ùna nic Choinnich takes him into the adit with a lamp. He tells her he has never seen the colours in the coal but can see the silver; she answers that the Dia-thìrich see it the same, and that this is why silver is not holy.

events.title: Death of Coinneach Glas
events.body: Coinneach Glas, Ceann a' Chùraim since the death of Tormod mac Ailein, dies in his chair in the room of the rolls at Cathair dhearg, aged sixty-nine, after twenty-four years in the seat. He has had Cùmhnant an Airgid read to him twice and called it a better paper than any he signed.

events.title: Alasdair Liath chosen Ceann a' Chùraim
events.body: Comhairle a' Chùraim chooses Alasdair Liath, aged forty-nine, to sit as Ceann a' Chùraim after Coinneach Glas. He has sat on the council since before Puingean a' Chalaidh and voted to sign them. The roll records his age and the number of voices and nothing more.

events.title: The first silver carts go down to Seann Bhral
events.body: Refusing the request of A' Chompanaidh that its silver pass through the quays of Ros dhomhain, Comann an Airgid sends its first carts of bar silver eighteen miles down the valley to Seann Bhral, and pays the port's custodians by the Muileann chiar weight on every bar. Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir tells the agent of A' Chompanaidh the compact gives no ground to object.

events.title: The guild's book of weighings filled
events.body: In the summer after the compact the smelting-floors of Muileann chiar work from dawn to dark, and the guild's paper book of the weighings, begun in An Aois Scaraidh and kept in a dozen hands, is filled by the autumn and a new one begun.

events.title: Ùna locks the compact in the guild chest
events.body: On the day Comann an Airgid reckons its year, the three keyholders open the guild chest and Cùmhnant an Airgid is read aloud in both tongues. Ùna nic Choinnich, aged fifty-nine, lays it back on the new book of weighings beside the notched boards of the old ledger, and the three locks are turned.

events.title: The guild enters the Baile gheal salt in its ledger
events.body: A carter from the west brings word to Muileann chiar that the carters of Baile gheal have taken up the Seann Warr salt trade round the lake. Ùna nic Choinnich has it written into the guild's new ledger as a thing the humans did not take.

events.title: The hearths of Àth dhearg take the tower on half-pay
events.body: The custodian of Àth dhearg calls the town's hearths to the room over the net-store. A' Chompanaidh will pay half the cost of a tower on the north-eastern cape in marks and send the lens and oil; the town is to find the stone and the hands, the other half of the pay being the promise that the light will bring its boats home. The town agrees.

events.title: Torcall's cairn set in the footing of the tower
events.body: The masons of Àth dhearg raise the tower over the old fire-shelf on the cape. They take down the cairn Torcall Clachair built there with James Fenn and set its stones in the footing, facing the sea, and turn a stair inside the wall. The old cut stair up the cliff is left as it was.

events.title: The first line of the Àth dhearg daybook
events.body: On the night of the lighting Tormod mac Pheadair, keeper of Taigh-solais Àth dhearg, writes the first line in the grey-bound book of the humans' paper that A' Chompanaidh left him: lit at dusk, the wind west and light, and no ship. It is the first keeper's daybook kept on the island.

events.title: Two dates at the head of the daybook
events.body: A man of A' Chompanaidh, unable to tell the days of passing ships from the nights of the moon, writes out the humans' months for the keeper of Àth dhearg. Thereafter Tormod mac Pheadair heads every entry with the humans' day above and the night of the moon beneath, and writes the humans' days in over his first entries.

events.title: The Àth dhearg boats brought home in the Bealltach gale
events.body: A north-easterly gale catches four boats of Àth dhearg on the long lines beyond the reef. The keeper lights the lamp an hour before dusk. Three boats come home by the light through the night, one from the wrong side of the reef; the fourth returns at dawn a man short. Tormod mac Pheadair enters the boats and the lost man by name.

events.title: The masons' pay entered in the roll of Àth dhearg
events.body: When A' Chompanaidh pays the eleven masons of the tower in marks at its foot, the custodian's clerk enters the payment in the town's roll, and beside it that the other half of their pay was made in the Bealltach gale, in four boats and three of them home.

events.title: The keeper of Àth dhearg sees the burning collier
events.body: Two nights after entering a laden collier of A' Chompanaidh going south, Tormod mac Pheadair sees a red light low in the south under the cloud from the middle watch until near dawn, and writes that he does not know what it was. The carters bring word four days later that raiders have burned her.

events.title: The keeper will not write the black boats
events.body: In Dubhlas a clerk of A' Chompanaidh rides to Àth dhearg to read the daybook and asks the keeper to write in black raiding boats seen going south before the burning. Tormod mac Pheadair answers that he saw none and will write no boat he has not seen. The clerk reports the book of no assistance.

events.title: The gunboat entered at Àth dhearg
events.body: In Teasach of the forty-seventh year a black two-masted ship of war of A' Chompanaidh, a gun in her bows under canvas and more men on deck than any trader carries, comes round the north coast and south past the cape. The keeper of Àth dhearg enters her with more care than any ship before.

events.title: The collier's crew fed near Ceann leathan
events.body: The raiders who burn the collier of A' Chompanaidh put her crew into their own boat and set them rowing for the land. The crew come ashore alive at a fishing village near Ceann leathan, where the households feed and shelter them until a rider can carry word south to Seann Bhral.

events.title: A' Chompanaidh charges Comann an Airgid with the burning
events.body: Within a month of the burning the agents of A' Chompanaidh say at Seann Bhral and Ros dhomhain, and write to Arthur Lisle, that Comann an Airgid paid the raiders in spite for the surveyors turned back from the adit at Muileann chiar. The guild makes no answer.

events.title: Àth dhearg lends two boats to Ceann leathan
events.body: A fisherman of Ceann leathan walks north nearly forty miles with two sons to ask Àth dhearg for a boat after the gunboat burns the cove. The households talk into the night and lend two, to be returned when Ceann leathan has built its own, and the three sail them south in Lùghnas.

events.title: The wall's footing on the shingle of Baile dhìreach
events.body: Promised timber by A' Chompanaidh, the yard-master Daniel Lusk asks the council of four at Baile dhìreach for a dry-stone wall up the town's shingle and lays its footing while they argue. The town's members hold that the shingle is kept and not built on. On the third night the stones are carried below the wrack-line.

events.title: The shingle clause read from both books
events.body: Nathan Cobb reads the compact of Baile dhìreach from the humans' book, where the shingle is the town's property; Iain Hale reads it from the Dia-thìris book, where the shingle is kept for the town. Asked by both sides which book is right, Iain Hale closes the book and says nothing.

events.title: The Hales keep their house at Baile dhìreach
events.body: When the council breaks and the human families leave for Ros bheag and Ros dhomhain, Samuel Hale, Eilidh nic Ruairidh and their son Iain stay in their house by the well at the head of the street. They take neither side on the wall and speak of other things when it is mentioned.

events.title: Iain Hale refuses the yard at Inis chrom
events.body: Daniel Lusk offers Iain Hale the foreman's place in the yard going to Inis chrom, for more marks than the yard has ever paid. After a night on the shingle and a talk with his father, Iain Hale refuses, and that winter builds the town's boats on the old slip by the town's leave.

events.title: The humans' book set back on the shelf
events.body: When the yard has sailed for Inis chrom, Iain Hale finds the council's book in the humans' tongue left open on the mending-table in the net-loft at Baile dhìreach, at a page with a date and nothing under it. He closes it and sets it back on the shelf beside the Dia-thìris book.

events.title: The rain fails in the Àth dhearg daybook
events.body: Through the spring and summer of the forty-eighth year the daybook of Àth dhearg records dry winds night after night, the fields inland yellow before midsummer, a heath fire of three days, and the burn below the town stopped, which it has never done in memory. Rain is written once in four months.

events.title: Tormod mac Pheadair reads the seed loan at Baile ruadh
events.body: Called by his wife's kin, the keeper of Àth dhearg walks to Baile ruadh and reads to its council, figure by figure, the terms in the humans' figures by which A' Chompanaidh's store at Seann Dunn lends seed corn for grain over five harvests. He finds the figures as the interpreter gave them.

events.title: Baile ruadh's seed debt entered
events.body: The custodians' roll of Baile ruadh enters the town's debt of seed corn to A' Chompanaidh under the night of the moon, with the measure and the five harvests, the first debt in grain to the strangers in any roll of the island. The clerk writes beside it the name of the keeper who read the figures.

events.title: Three students carry the question west
events.body: In the autumn three students of Taigh na Deasbaid at Dùn thais walk over the high moor to Baile Mòr uaine, carrying Aonghas mac Coinnich's question with a sealed copy in the register-keeper's hand. The masters of Baile Mòr uaine take it up at the dark of the year.

events.title: The four hundred leaves come back to Dùn thais
events.body: The record of the argument at Baile Mòr uaine comes back to Dùn thais leaf by leaf with the carriers, four hundred leaves in all. Its last leaf lists those who spoke and notes that the hall adjourned because the peat was done. Aonghas mac Coinnich reads every leaf and names no argument the best.

events.title: Eachann Mòr loses his seat
events.body: The council at Cathair dhearg protests Cairt Chathair gheal, which names no custodian, and receives an answer in the humans' tongue that none of its members can read with confidence. At the autumn choosing at Ceann àrsaidh the households put out Eachann Mòr, who has no letters of that tongue, and choose Dùghall Òg of the carting families, who worked five years at A' Chompanaidh's weigh-house.

events.title: Cnoc ghorm stops selling grain
events.body: Through the first winter the villagers of Cnoc ghorm sell grain at a fair price to the human farmers who have cleared land beside them, and carry it on their own ponies. When the farmers' mill turns in the spring, they sell no more, and give no reason. Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's letters speak of a coolness at the old village.

events.title: Calum's ship sails north-about
events.body: Calum, son of Eachann Mòr, thirteen years old, goes aboard a ship of A' Chompanaidh at the quay below Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir at Ros dhomhain with Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's letter and a purse of marks sewn into his coat. A pilot of Caol leathan takes her down the Abhainn gheal on the evening tide, and she turns north up the west coast to go round by the north to the humans' land.

events.title: Eachann Mòr's first letter over the sea
events.body: No letter comes from Calum by the autumn ships. In the winter Eachann Mòr writes to his son in Dia-thìris, pays a pupil of Scoil na Teachdaireachd to put it into the humans' tongue beneath his lines, and gives it with a mark to the master of the first ship going north. No answer comes to it, nor to the three he sends after it.

events.title: Ciorstaidh nic Eachainn at the school of Inis bhàn
events.body: Eachann Mòr sends his daughter Ciorstaidh, ten years old, to the custodians' new school at Inis bhàn. She comes home at midsummer able to name forty hills and to argue the boundaries of her father's parish. The custodians of Inis bhàn keep Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's complaint about their pupils as a testimonial.

events.title: The students at Drochaid Ros fhionn
events.body: Aonghas mac Coinnich takes the students of Dùn thais to watch the first coal-carts cross the rebuilt bridge at Ros fhionn, forty in an afternoon. The island's drivers throw down lumps for them to name; the two human drivers look at their loads as at stones. Ailean Clachair's sign stays in the keystone.

events.title: The passenger line read at A' Chompanaidh's counter
events.body: In the third year after his son sailed Eachann Mòr asks at A' Chompanaidh's counter at Ros dhomhain after the ship by name. She has come and gone twice since, under another master now. Against the day Calum sailed the clerk reads one line, a native boy, his fare paid in full, and says his book knows nothing more.

events.title: Caol gharbh's letter on the door at Dùn thais
events.body: Aonghas mac Coinnich pins a copy of the letter of Caol gharbh's custodians, who wrote that they had not known a town could be harmed by a road it was not on, to the door of Taigh na Deasbaid at Dùn thais beside the carved lintel. It stays there until the rain takes it.

events.title: The search party returns from Doire uaine
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's search party of eight men goes up into the hills of Doire uaine and comes down the same evening. They report the lost surveyors' chains laid out along a ridge and a ring of fire-stones with no ash in it, and refuse to go further for pay or threats. The agent writes to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir that the men are idle.

events.title: Eachann Mòr asks the question at Dùn thais
events.body: At the end of harvest Eachann Mòr rides two days from Ceann àrsaidh to Dùn thais and asks Aonghas mac Coinnich whether his son, five years among the humans, will see the colour in the coal when he comes home. The master puts a broken lump in his hand and will not answer. The register records that a man came to ask the question and the master did not answer it.

events.title: Anne Colby lands at Ros dhomhain
events.body: Anne Colby comes ashore at the Ros dhomhain quays at two and twenty, sent out by Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise with a chest of linen and instruments she has scarcely been shown how to use, hoping to hear word of a brother lost years before on Harrow's ships. She finds no word of him; within the year she finds the flux.

events.title: Barabal nic Dhùghaill reads the schedule at Cathair dhearg
events.body: A pupil of Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise of fifteen, Barabal nic Dhùghaill, renders Lisle's three sealed sheets into Dia-thìris before the council, reading the new fraction twice over at the old custodian of Cnoc bheag's asking. The council has her rendering copied word for word into every coal town's roll, with her own name set at the foot of each copy.

events.title: The tithe on the tithe named at Dùn fhiadhaich
events.body: Griogair Fada, the largest farmer under Cnoc naomh, asks the young tithe-gatherer who set the new weight on grain and gets no answer he can carry home. The custodians of Dùn fhiadhaich enter the weighing in their roll under a name of their own coining, deachamh an deachaimh, the tithe on the tithe.

events.title: A' Chompanaidh's surgeon visits once
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's own surgeon comes to the chapel door at Ros dhomhain, will not step past the threshold, and tells Colby she would do better to let the sick lie where they were found. He sends, before he leaves the harbour, a case of salts and does not come again.

events.title: Mòr nic Amhlaidh's counsel on names
events.body: Washing the chapel floor by lamplight on Colby's first night of nursing the flux, the widow Mòr nic Amhlaidh tells her that the dying want their own names said to them more than they want the fever broken. Colby is said to have kept the counsel from that night on.

events.title: Colby turns the chapel into a sick-house
events.body: Anne Colby has Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's chapel at Ros dhomhain opened and its benches carried into the yard without asking anyone's leave, and with Mòr nic Amhlaidh and her daughter carries the flux-sick up from the harbour lodgings on a hand-barrow until the stone room and its yard hold as many as can lie down.

events.title: Colby's roll of the dead by name
events.body: Each evening Anne Colby sits at the chapel door with the custodians' own roll open on her knee and a clerk's boy to read her the entries, and sets down against every name who lived and who died, in English, in a column she turns round on the table for the custodians to see is kept.

events.title: A bargeman put ashore at Seann Vell
events.body: A bargeman on the coal run east from Ros dhomhain falls sick at his pole and is put ashore at the Seann Vell landing rather than carried on, the barge-master judging, wrongly, that dry land would serve him better than the water. Within the month the flux is in a dozen houses of the town.

events.title: Seann Vell shuts its landing
events.body: The custodians of Seann Vell, led by Mairead nic Amhlaidh, close the only quay their river town has for the coal traffic that feeds it, and let no barge tie up there through a whole season, though the closing costs the town every fee that quay has ever earned it.

events.title: A' Chompanaidh fines Seann Vell for the shut landing
events.body: A letter from the pay office fines Seann Vell for the season's lost landing fees and says nothing of the flux the closing was meant to check. Mairead nic Amhlaidh reads it to the town council on the landing steps within sight of that season's graves, and the town pays it from the same purse that buried its dead.

events.title: Arthur Lisle dies at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir
events.body: Arthur Lisle dies at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir above Ros dhomhain of a fever that settles in his chest and then his heart, a fortnight dying by inches and signing papers to the last. He is one and sixty, Àrd-mhaor twenty years, remembered by the custodians for a raised voice never once heard at their council table, though not forgiven the schedule.

events.title: Uisdean Ruadh's first walk to Ceann mhin
events.body: Uisdean Ruadh, a hewer of Muileann chrom, walks with forty of his gang before light on a morning of frost to stand in the pay line at Ceann mhin till near dusk, and walks home again in the dark. He keeps the cost of it afterward on a notched stick, kept still by his family three generations on.

events.title: Raghnall Maor buried beside the eleven
events.body: Raghnall Maor is buried on the hill above Muileann chrom beside the eleven of his first gallery, in thin rain, with both shifts of the pit standing at the grave together, a thing not done for any death there before. Anne Colby stands at the grave's edge with her roll and adds, that evening, a line naming his office, the only such line the roll holds.

events.title: Raghnall Maor dies at Muileann chrom
events.body: Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, called Raghnall Maor, dies at two and seventy in the slate-roofed house A' Chompanaidh built him above the pit he first walked as a guide. Anne Colby, sent for by his son, sits with him two nights before the end; he asks her once whether she writes her dead down by name and tells her it is a good thing to keep doing.

events.title: A' Chompanaidh gives Dòmhnall his father's staff
events.body: Within the week of the burying a clerk from Ceann mhin brings Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill the office, the slate roof and the crews together as one paper needing only his mark. The custodians of Muileann chrom, who had hoped the office might die with Raghnall, see it pass from father to son as if it had always been meant to.

events.title: Edwin Lowe sent to Muileann bheag
events.body: Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise sends the cleric Edwin Lowe up from Ros dhomhain to look into a complaint laid by the keepers of the new Taigh-solais Muileann bheag. He rides three days by mule-track and a fourth along the open coast, and finds the beacon burning coal, the first of the island's lights to do so.
